passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites and tell them this is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Anyone from the house of Israel who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat in the camp or outside of it instead of bringing it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before His tabernacle—that man shall incur bloodguilt. He has shed blood and must be cut off from among his people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Aaron.
Aaron was the high priest.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Aaron’s sons.
Aaron’s sons were priests.
The LORD told Moses to speak to all the Israelites.
The LORD said, “This is what I command you to say.”
Any man from the house of Israel who kills an ox, a lamb, or a goat in the camp must follow this command.
Any man from the house of Israel who kills an ox, a lamb, or a goat outside the camp must also follow this command.
If a man does not bring the animal to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, he disobeys the LORD.
The Tent of Meeting was the place of worship.
The man must bring the animal as an offering to the LORD.
The offering must be presented before the LORD’s tabernacle.
If the man does not do this, he is guilty of shedding blood.
The LORD will count him as one who has shed blood.
That man must be cut off from his people.
He will no longer be part of the community of Israel.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְאֶל־ בָּנָ֗יו וְאֶל֙ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ אִ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁחַ֜ט שׁ֥וֹר אוֹ־ כֶ֛שֶׂב אוֹ־ עֵ֖ז בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה א֚וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשְׁחַ֔ט מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃ וְאֶל־ פֶּ֜תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵד֮ לֹ֣א הֱבִיאוֹ֒ לְהַקְרִ֤יב קָרְבָּן֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֑ה דָּ֣ם יֵחָשֵׁ֞ב לָאִ֤ישׁ הַהוּא֙ דָּ֣ם שָׁפָ֔ךְ וְנִכְרַ֛ת הָאִ֥ישׁ הַה֖וּא מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For this reason the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they have been offering in the open fields. They are to bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and offer them as sacrifices of peace to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites are God's chosen people.
God gave them laws through Moses.
God commanded the Israelites to bring their sacrifices to Him.
The Israelites had been offering sacrifices in the open fields.
God told them to stop sacrificing in the fields.
They must bring their sacrifices to the LORD.
They must come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
They must bring the sacrifices to the priest.
The priest will offer the sacrifices to the LORD.
These sacrifices will be peace offerings to the LORD.
passages.original: לְמַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָבִ֜יאוּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶֽת־ זִבְחֵיהֶם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵ֣ם זֹבְחִים֮ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶה֒ וֶֽהֱבִיאֻ֣ם לַֽיהוָ֗ה אֶל־ פֶּ֛תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְזָ֨בְח֜וּ זִבְחֵ֧י שְׁלָמִ֛ים לַֽיהוָ֖ה אוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: The priest will then sprinkle the blood on the altar of the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The priest is a servant of God.
The priest stands at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest takes the blood from the sacrifice.
The priest sprinkles the blood on the altar of the LORD.
The altar stands at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest takes the fat from the sacrifice.
The priest burns the fat on the altar.
The burning fat makes a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.original: וְזָרַ֨ק הַכֹּהֵ֤ן אֶת־ הַדָּם֙ עַל־ מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְהִקְטִ֣יר הַחֵ֔לֶב לְרֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat demons to which they have prostituted themselves. This will be a permanent statute for them for the generations to come.’
passages.sermon:
The Israelites must not offer their sacrifices to goat demons.
These goat demons are false gods.
The Israelites have turned away from God to follow these demons.
God commands them to stop this practice.
This command will last forever.
This rule will apply to all their future generations.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ יִזְבְּח֥וּ עוֹד֙ אֶת־ זִבְחֵיהֶ֔ם לַשְּׂעִירִ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם זֹנִ֖ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֛ם תִּֽהְיֶה־ זֹּ֥את לָהֶ֖ם לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Tell them that if anyone from the house of Israel or any foreigner living among them offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice but does not bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to sacrifice it to the LORD, that man must be cut off from his people.
passages.sermon:
God gave a command to Moses for the Israelites and the foreigners living among them.
God said, “Tell the Israelites and the foreigners living with them this law.
If any person from the house of Israel offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
or if any foreigner living among them offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
and that person does not bring the offering to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
and that person does not bring the sacrifice to the LORD at the entrance,
then that person must be cut off from his people.”
passages.original: וַאֲלֵהֶ֣ם תֹּאמַ֔ר אִ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִן־ הַגֵּ֖ר אֲשֶׁר־ יָג֣וּר בְּתוֹכָ֑ם אֲשֶׁר־ יַעֲלֶ֥ה עֹלָ֖ה אוֹ־ זָֽבַח׃ וְאֶל־ פֶּ֜תַח אֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ לֹ֣א יְבִיאֶ֔נּוּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת אֹת֖וֹ לַיהוָ֑ה וְנִכְרַ֛ת הָאִ֥ישׁ הַה֖וּא מֵעַמָּֽיו׃

passages.text: If anyone from the house of Israel or a foreigner living among them eats any blood, I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to the Israelites and to foreigners living among them.
If any person from the house of Israel eats any blood, God will act against that person.
If any foreigner living among the Israelites eats any blood, God will act against that person.
God will turn His face against the person who eats blood.
God will cut that person off from among his people.
passages.original: וְאִ֨ישׁ אִ֜ישׁ מִבֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וּמִן־ הַגֵּר֙ הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֹאכַ֖ל כָּל־ דָּ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֣י פָנַ֗י בַּנֶּ֙פֶשׁ֙ הָאֹכֶ֣לֶת אֶת־ הַדָּ֔ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י אֹתָ֖הּ מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement for your souls upon the altar; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God gave them laws about sacrifices and blood.
The life of every living body is in its blood.
God gave blood to the Israelites for a special purpose.
God commanded them to use blood on the altar.
Blood on the altar makes atonement for their souls.
Blood brings forgiveness for the soul.
Blood is necessary for atonement.
passages.original: כִּ֣י נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַבָּשָׂר֮ בַּדָּ֣ם הִוא֒ וַאֲנִ֞י נְתַתִּ֤יו לָכֶם֙ עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ לְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־ נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ הַדָּ֥ם ה֖וּא בַּנֶּ֥פֶשׁ יְכַפֵּֽר׃

passages.text: Therefore I say to the Israelites, ‘None of you may eat blood, nor may any foreigner living among you eat blood.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God gave them a command.
God said, "None of you may eat blood."
God also spoke to the foreigners living among the Israelites.
God said, "No foreigner living among you may eat blood."
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֤ן אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כָּל־ נֶ֥פֶשׁ מִכֶּ֖ם לֹא־ תֹ֣אכַל דָּ֑ם וְהַגֵּ֛ר הַגָּ֥ר בְּתוֹכְכֶ֖ם לֹא־ יֹ֥אכַל דָּֽם׃ס

passages.text: And if any Israelite or foreigner living among them hunts down a wild animal or bird that may be eaten, he must drain its blood and cover it with dirt.
passages.sermon:
Any Israelite may hunt a wild animal or a bird that is allowed for food.
Any foreigner living among the Israelites may also hunt such animals or birds.
If a person hunts a wild animal or a bird that can be eaten, he must drain its blood.
He must pour out the blood.
He must cover the blood with dirt.
passages.original: וְאִ֨ישׁ אִ֜ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וּמִן־ הַגֵּר֙ הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצ֜וּד צֵ֥יד חַיָּ֛ה אוֹ־ ע֖וֹף אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵאָכֵ֑ל וְשָׁפַךְ֙ אֶת־ דָּמ֔וֹ וְכִסָּ֖הוּ בֶּעָפָֽר׃

passages.text: For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I have told the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any living thing, because the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God said, “I am the LORD your God.”
The life of every living creature is in its blood.
I told the Israelites this truth.
You must not eat the blood of any creature.
The blood is the life of every creature.
Anyone who eats blood will be cut off.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל־ בָּשָׂ֗ר דָּמ֣וֹ בְנַפְשׁוֹ֮ הוּא֒ וָֽאֹמַר֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל דַּ֥ם כָּל־ בָּשָׂ֖ר לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ כִּ֣י נֶ֤פֶשׁ כָּל־ בָּשָׂר֙ דָּמ֣וֹ הִ֔וא כָּל־ אֹכְלָ֖יו יִכָּרֵֽת׃

passages.text: And any person, whether native or foreigner, who eats anything found dead or mauled by wild beasts must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening; then he will be clean.
passages.sermon:
This law applies to any person among the Israelites or foreigners living with them.
If a person eats an animal that was found dead or killed by wild beasts, this law applies to him.
He must wash his clothes.
He must bathe himself in water.
He will be unclean until evening.
After evening, he will be clean.
passages.original: וְכָל־ נֶ֗פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֹּאכַ֤ל נְבֵלָה֙ וּטְרֵפָ֔ה בָּאֶזְרָ֖ח וּבַגֵּ֑ר וְכִבֶּ֨ס בְּגָדָ֜יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֛יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־ הָעֶ֖רֶב וְטָהֵֽר׃

passages.text: But if he does not wash his clothes and bathe himself, then he shall bear his iniquity.”
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to the Israelites.
God told them what to do if they ate an animal that died or was killed by wild beasts.
God said they must wash their clothes.
God said they must bathe themselves in water.
If a person does not wash his clothes,
and if he does not bathe himself,
then he will be guilty.
He will bear his own sin.
passages.original: וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א יְכַבֵּ֔ס וּבְשָׂר֖וֹ לֹ֣א יִרְחָ֑ץ וְנָשָׂ֖א עֲוֺנֽוֹ׃פ
